exclude: CPU port, zero-page working registers, stack and KERNAL work RAM. The tape bootstrap starts at $0316 and the game blocks supply no authored bytes here.
KERNAL vectors overwritten by the tape bootstrap.
KERNAL tape header and residual bootstrap workspace; no bytes here are part of the nine game blocks.
Residual KERNAL tape header and bootstrap, up to the game payload at $0400.
At hand-over this is the relocated tape loader and its workspace. The game overwrites it with generated screen cells and live sprite pointers.
extra: Game turbo block 8 after the loader copies it to $A000, and block 9.
Game turbo block 5, including the title picture.
Source image of turbo block 8 below I/O.

comments.text: Three little-endian packed BCD bytes for the player score. $C5C3 adds to them and $C5E7 displays them as six digits.
The middle two digits of the live score, stored in BCD.
The most significant two score digits. The extra-life check uses bit 1 of this BCD byte.
Three little-endian BCD pairs supplied by the front end and drawn by $C608.
The middle BCD pair returned by the front end to initialize the high-score display.
Most significant BCD pair for the high score.
Sets the VIC-II horizontal control to $18 and jumps into the title initializer.
Jumps to the front end's post-game handler at $04FC.
Jumps to $0461, which packs six displayed high-score digits into three bytes for the fight engine.
Jumps to the screen setup at $0411, which saves A and blanks the display before clearing screen and color cells.
Subtracts the screen-code zero from each of six stored score digits and packs each pair into BCD. Returns the most significant pair in X, the middle pair in Y, and the least significant pair in A.
Installs the RAM NMI pointer, initializes the music driver, draws the bitmap title and jumps into the attract loop.
Patches the operand of BIT at $0524 to CIA2 port A and restores it afterwards. A clear DATA input bit calls the second memory exchange at $1C03, which replaces part of the game engine image.
Operand byte temporarily set to $DD by the serial DATA check. The following instructions restore it to $D0 and branch using the saved input flag.
Copies the four TIME characters to the bottom row and uses X to set their color.
Copies the 24-character name-entry prompt and inserts the player digit at $4044.
Subtracts the CIA1 time-of-day minutes from the decimal deadline and displays the two resulting digits.
Configures the CIA1 clock rate from the PAL flag and clears its time-of-day registers before setting its alarm path.
Player-number offset inserted in the end-of-game and name-entry prompts.
Four PETSCII characters supplying the name-entry countdown label.
Eighteen characters for the end-of-game player heading. $0535 adds the player digit.
Name-entry prompt lettering, copied to the menu screen as low-six-bit character codes.
Source of the 24 displayed name-entry prompt characters, starting at the E of ENTER.
Saves the stage and player arguments, disables sprites and expands the current BCD score into the front end's six-digit comparison buffer.
Increments the border color register and jumps back to itself. The loop has no in-code exit.
Writes 250 white color cells per bank segment across all 1,000 visible cells.
The column labels for the rank, score, stage and name display.
Compares the current score with saved entries from the bottom of the rank table upward. Moves six-digit scores and the associated name and stage fields together as it inserts the entry.
Begins another bottom-up comparison pass with the last rank index and clears the movement flag.
Compares adjacent rank scores digit by digit. Returns at the first difference, leaving its carry for the ranking sort.
Builds $DD and $9C using XOR, patches the high operand of the store at $0714 and writes $9C to CIA2 port A on the setup pass. Restores the operand to $D0 afterward.
Immediate byte XORed with $55 to form the serial setup store's high address.
Immediate byte XORed with $E9 to form the port value.
High byte of the store that applies the serial port setup. $070D patches it to $DD during setup and $0719 restores it to $D0.
Cleared at the start of a ranking pass and tested to decide whether another pass is needed.
Current comparison row, decremented from nine toward zero.
Ten groups of six ASCII-form digits used when comparing, inserting or drawing ranked scores.
Second digit of the leading rank score.
Third digit of the leading rank score.
Fourth digit of the leading rank score.
Fifth digit of the leading rank score.
Sixth digit of the leading rank score.
Base for the adjacent record in the six-digit comparison at $0703.
Six display digits for the just-finished game, expanded from packed BCD before the rank comparison.
Ten slots of ten characters for the name entry and rank table.
Ten characters cleared to spaces before the new score is inserted.
Five-character stage fields for the saved ranks, followed by the small working tail for the current result.
Stage number saved from the round result for the rank display.
Ten pointers to rank name slots in reverse order, used to choose the new name-entry destination.
Zero before ranking, then updated on an insertion and used to choose which name slot to edit.
The screen-code letter currently selected in the joystick name editor.
Scratch for packing two score digits and for preserving Y while servicing sound.
Copy of the displayed character used by the name-entry loop.
Draws the standings and player prompt. Looks up the destination for the inserted name in the row-pointer table, then runs the joystick name-entry loop.
Services the music and repeats the name preview while polling the joystick. Writes the selected screen code to the current character position.
Waits for raster low byte $FF, advances sound, polls the joystick and checks the serial data line. Fire enters the player menu, while the counter alternates the title bitmap and credits.
Waits for the raster, blanks and clears the old picture, switches to VIC bank $4000 and begins drawing the one- or two-player prompt.

The operand at this store starts the menu clear-and-draw sequence after the bank and charset are set. Clears the border, background and input latch, then expands the selected menu text into screen RAM.
Low part of the attract timing count, also used as a raster-delay counter on the menu paths.
The high byte of the two-byte attract-screen countdown.
Alternates the attract sequence between the bitmap title and credit text.
Selects the $7000 text charset in VIC bank $4000 and starts the standings at $4078. Each rank row uses the separate saved name, packed score digits and stage fields.
Calculates table offsets from the rank index, copies the name and six score digits into the current display row, and advances through the saved ranks.
Row counter for the rank text builder, reused as an offset scratch in the ranking sort.
Holds the countdown while emitting the rows of the rank display.
Scratch holding the doubled rank row while the printer computes six times the row index.
Selects VIC bank $C000 and multicolor bitmap mode, with pixels at $E000 and screen attributes at $CC00. Copies the title's per-cell color RAM source from $C800.
ANDs the active-low states read at CIA1 ports A and B, then inverts them. Keeps the fire bit for changed samples and strips it from unchanged samples, retaining the direction bits.
Last combined joystick sample from both ports, used to suppress repeated fire.
The menu's normalized input bits, with repeated fire removed.
Waits for raster low byte $FF, ticks the music, and decrements the delay counter at $0A87 until zero. Reloads the counter with three and preserves Y across the music call.
Writes spaces to all four screen pages at $4000 and writes color 3 to the corresponding four color RAM pages.
Source for the Konami and Imagine credits and the C64 development names. Viewed as characters after masking the top two bits.
The instructions for one- and two-player selection and their labels, copied into the player menu.
Adjacent menu option fields copied into the one- or two-player selection row.
The menu text for the perfect-round bonus and the extra life, including spaces for screen layout.
Menu text ending with the instruction to press the fire button to start.
The menu's 31-character fire-to-start instruction.
Copies the first 80 credit bytes from $0C0F, masks each to a screen code and writes both the cells and color 4. The rest of the routine adds the remaining credit text.
Buchu’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 0. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
Star’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 1. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
This address is inside Star's copied parameter record. It also appears as the discarded BIT address in an overlapping sound-command entry.
Nuncha’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 2. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
Pole’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 3. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.

Fan’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 6. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
Sword’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 7. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
This address is inside Sword's copied parameter record. The song selector's overlapping BIT instruction incidentally names it.
Tonfun’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 8. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
Blues’s 223-byte record copied to $B65F for opponent index 9. The first arrays select three component sprites per pose, followed by the position offsets, attack parameters and sprite color.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the first sprite. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the second sprite. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the third sprite. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the first y. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the second y. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the third y. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the first x. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the second x. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Seventeen Oolong pose entries for the third x. The active move maps into these arrays via $1A99 before $BC00 or $BC71 places the three sprite pieces.
Maps the five-bit Oolong move code to a pose index for the sprite parts and offsets at $1A00.
Four vertical contact offsets per pose. $A54E and $A5D1 add them to the player origin before comparing against a target.
Horizontal contact offsets addressed from the player pose and transformed when the fighters swap facing.
Flags indexed by pose or move by the contact routines to select which geometry can attack or block.
Jumps into the stage-screen stream decoder. A chooses an entry from the source-pointer table at $1CBA.
Jumps to the block exchange routine at $1CC2. Where this code block continues, $1C06 masks the stream selector for the alternative decode path.
Reads the next source byte, sending values below $FB to the cell writer. Commands $FB through $FF dispatch through the word table at $1C75 using a self-modified JSR.
Low operand byte of the stream decoder's patchable JSR.
High operand byte of the stream decoder's patchable JSR.
Reads the byte at the source cursor in $FD/$FE and increments the cursor, carrying between pages.
Writes a glyph to the screen cursor, maps its page to color RAM, writes the current color, and advances the original screen cursor.
Five handler addresses in order from $FB (repeat glyph) through $FF (leave the decoder), used to patch the call at $1C44.
Takes a run length then a glyph byte from the stream. Calls the cell writer once per glyph, with a zero length running for 256 iterations.
Reads two stream bytes and installs them as the low and high destination cursor.
Reads the next byte as the color saved for subsequent cells.
Drops the return address of the stream dispatch call and returns to the caller of the decoder.
Advances the encoded source cursor by 20 with carry.
Holds the glyph byte used by the repeat command.
Current color for newly decoded screen cells.
Temporarily saves the character-page high byte while the screen stream writer selects color RAM.
Four source pointers in selector order. They name the waterfall scenery, temple scenery, score panel and opponent preview streams.
A=0 swaps $2000–$307E with $5300–$637E. A=1 swaps $0400–$0FFF with $A000–$ABFF. Exchanges full pages and then the trailing bytes with $F2 as scratch.
Immediate operand set by the block exchange routine to the number of bytes in its trailing partial page.
Start addresses for the left operand of the two in-place block swaps at $1CC2.
Start addresses for the right operand of the two in-place block swaps at $1CC2.
Each pair gives the trailing byte count then the number of full pages to exchange.
First 16 component sprites in the exchange bank. Each 64-byte slot has 21 rows of three bytes plus a trailing byte. The first slots draw body and stance pieces.
The trailing byte of the first sprite slot in the swap bank doubles as the bank marker. $BDB7 checks it to decide whether to exchange with $5300.
Interior of the slot at $2380 in the component sprite exchange bank. The sound selector also names this as an incidental BIT operand.
Component sprites 16–31 in the $2000 exchange bank. They include bent legs and raised arms for assembling poses.
Component sprites 32–47 in the $2000 exchange bank, including heads, torso poses and detached limb pieces.
Interior of slot $2980. The underlying exchange-bank sprite bytes continue through $29BF, followed by the later component shapes.
Component sprites 48–63 in the $2000 exchange bank, including small forms and extended diagonal limbs.
Interior of the slot at $2F80 in the late sprites of the exchange bank, coincident with one sound selector's BIT operand.
The final two sprite slots in the $2000 exchange bank. The $1CC2 exchange copies through $307E, ending at the last bitmap byte.
Encoded preview glyph data with FB runs and FE colors. This 257-byte fragment also occurs at $3662.
A 155-byte run of encoded stage commands and tiles identical to the run beginning at $3763 and part of the waterfall stream.
Encoded screen data ending in $FF. Starts below the score panel at $4078 and writes the NEXT OPPONENT caption and preview cards.
Encoded preview-card tile and name commands after the first $FF terminator of the preview stream. The opening 188 bytes also occur at $3445.
Encoded rock color and glyph commands copied from $3506 after the preview data.
Encoded screen data ending in $FF. Starts at $4078 and fills 881 cells with the temple backdrop and ground.
Encoded score panel, 120 cells from $4000 through $4077. Includes player, high score, level, lives, Oolong, Buchu and the two KO bars.
Encoded color changes and terrain glyph runs lying between the score-panel stream terminator and the first waterfall command.
Encoded screen data ending in $FF. Starts at $4078 and fills 881 cells with the waterfall scenery and ground.
Encoded repeats of the waterfall area's turquoise-floor tile commands after the first terminator. This includes repeated runs of spaces and terrain glyphs.
Four consecutive $E4–$E7 bytes following the waterfall screen stream. The stream terminates earlier at $3FCB.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $10–$1F. The rendered group includes folded and extended arms alongside stance pieces.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $20–$2F. The rendered group includes turned torsos and separate stepping legs.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $30–$3F. The rendered group includes long leg silhouettes and low body pieces.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $40–$4F. The rendered group includes the opening slots of the $5300 exchange area.
Begins the 4,223-byte exchange bank used by $1CC2. It occupies parts of nearby sprite groups and swaps with $2000–$307E for the other opponent group.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $50–$5F. The rendered group includes legs and torsos with multicolor outlines.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $60–$6F. The rendered group includes arm thrusts and compact body pieces.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $70–$7F. The rendered group includes standing legs and front-facing body pieces.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $80–$8F. The rendered group includes long horizontal pieces near the end of the exchange.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $90–$9F. The rendered group includes thin horizontal or diagonal pieces and helmet-like shapes.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $A0–$AF. The rendered group includes rounded shields and broad bent leg pieces.
VIC bank $4000 sprite slots $B0–$BF. The rendered group includes small weapon pieces, hand silhouettes and stance components.
Biased destination operand for the third byte of each reflected weapon row in sprite slot $BB.
Third column address for one of the reflected fighter pieces. The copier writes the reflected shape in the $6F00 slot.
Biased destination for the third column of each reflected row in the $6F40 buffer.
Biased destination for the third column of each reflected row in the $6F80 buffer.
Sprite slot $BF. The direction updater at $B8E0 replaces eight pixel bytes starting at slot byte one with the selected glyph.
First 128 8-byte glyphs for the waterfall set. Codes $01–$1A are upper-case letters and $30–$39 are digits. Codes from $40 also carry screen decoration.
Base address for eight-byte direction images. $B8E0 copies the rows selected by the offset table at $B904 into sprite slot $BF.
Glyphs following the direction icon source. This range includes numeral screen codes $30–$39 and additional tile patterns.
Upper 128 glyphs in the waterfall set, including multicolor rock, water and edge patterns used by the stage tile map.
Low half of the second 256-glyph set. The opening patterns include compact multicolor tile pieces alongside the repeated $00 glyph.
High half of the second 256-glyph set, with tiles for edges and repeating stage textures.
Uses even Y offsets as command numbers. Loads the selected handler address from $800F, overwrites the jump operand, and jumps with the handler address high byte in A.
Low byte of the handler address patched by the public SID dispatcher.
High byte of the handler address patched by the public SID dispatcher.
The command dispatcher accepts an even Y offset into this table of 25 handler addresses. The first handler advances voices, and the next entries include mute, busy status, and volume.
Base used by $8006 for the high bytes in the interleaved command address table.
Starts the SID effect components from $8ED1 and $8EF0 and $8F0F through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $90A2 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect components from $9045 and $9026 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect components from $8F4D and $8F6C through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $8EB2 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $8FC9 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $9007 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect components from $8F8B and $8FAA through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $8FE8 through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect component from $8F2E through the common effect queue routine.
Starts the SID effect components from $9083 and $9064 through the common effect queue routine.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $05 of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $0B of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $11 of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $17 of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $1D of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $23 of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $29 of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Loads Y with the final byte offset $2F of the selected stream-pointer group. The overlapping BIT instructions skip the later LDY operands.
Selects the last three stream pointers in the title song group before the common song setup copies each pointer and resets its state.
ORs the three song-stream flags and three effects flags. Callers use zero to wait for the sound driver to finish.
Clears song and effect activity, writes zero to all three SID voice register groups and sets the driver voice state bytes at $8D52–$8D54 to $FF.
Caches X as the volume contribution and writes filter and volume registers.
Copies the cached filter cutoff and resonance and ORs the selected filter mode with the volume for $D418.
Saves X as a mask used by the note parser to select restart behavior on the channels.
Loads two cached pitch bytes and saves them to the active voice 1 modulation state.
Restores the two modulation counters from voice 1's saved synthesis parameters.
Loads two cached pitch bytes into the voice 2 effect's active modulation state.
Stores the cached voice 2 ramp counts as the active counters.
Loads and saves cached frequency bytes for the third SID voice's active effect.
Loads the two active voice 3 modulation counters from their saved values.
Sets X to zero and enters the common effect setup at $81CA. The incoming A and Y hold the low and high bytes of the effect descriptor address.
Saves the effect descriptor pointer and channel number, loads the SID voice's starting registers from the descriptor, then copies remaining state fields for the effect service routine.
Patched register displacement used when selecting the SID voice for the effect descriptor's initialization.
Operand byte inside the effect register store. The effect setup that uses it loads values from the descriptor and clears the test bit for the control register write.
Copies the saved voice 1 note frequency into the effect oscillator state, then reloads its modulation parameters.
Copies four saved modulation bytes for voice 1.
Copies the current voice 2 note frequency into the effect oscillator state and reloads modulation parameters.
Copies four modulation bytes for voice 2.
Copies the current voice 3 note frequency into the effect oscillator state and reloads modulation parameters.
Copies four modulation bytes for voice 3.
Services filter setup and the other two voices. Decrements voice 1's duration, and reads another event when it expires.
Reads the next voice 1 event. Values $C0 or above index command handlers, and lower values encode a note or rest with a following duration byte.
Low operand of the jump that dispatches voice 1's song event handler.
High operand byte inside the patchable voice 1 command jump. The following note path instead reads the duration and pitch data before advancing the stream.
Increments the repeat stack cursor. Restores the saved stream pointer unless the cursor is back at eight, when it clears the voice's playing flag.
Saves a return position and count on voice 1's repeat stack, steps the stack cursor down and advances to the next event.
Decrements the current repeat counter and returns to the saved stream position while the count remains. On completion pops the repeat state and advances one byte.
Copies five bytes from the event's descriptor into $8C40–$8C44 and advances to the next command.
Copies 14 bytes from the instrument record to $8C28, then advances the stream. The alternate $8421 entry copies ten bytes instead.
Loads the shared copy loop's Y index with nine for a ten-byte instrument record.
Reads a parameter source from the command stream, copies into the indexed voice workspace and advances the event pointer by five bytes.
Reads the following byte as a new transposition and updates the voice 1 stream cursor to the address from the command.
Stores X and A as the new voice 1 stream cursor, then reads an event at that address.
Pushes a return address that resumes at the voice 1 stream advance, then jumps through the pointer at $0016.
Changes transposition, saves the stream address four bytes ahead on the repeat stack, and starts decoding at the supplied target.
Saves a return point three bytes ahead before branching to the same pointer replacement as the transpose command.
Updates $8D4C from X and advances by the one-operand command length.
Stores A by index into the voice 1 instrument parameters and advances three bytes.
Updates an indexed byte of voice 1 effect state and advances the music stream.
Services the first voice's effect if its counter is nonzero. Controls note gate timing and lets the following paths update the oscillator.
Returns without another update.
Steps through three pitch ramps. Each selects a 16-bit delta while its duration remains and passes the resulting oscillator value to $85D3.
Writes the updated two-byte frequency to the first SID oscillator and its cached copy.
Decrements the duration of voice 2 and reads a new event when due. The effect-service path runs while the current event still has time remaining.
Low operand of the jump that dispatches voice 2 song events.
High operand byte inside the voice 2 command jump. The note path that follows translates duration, notes, rests and transposition for voice 2.
Voice 2 command $C0. Pops a stream frame, restoring the saved address or clearing the voice playing flag when the stack is empty.
Voice 2 command $CC. Saves a repeat count and a stream return position, then changes the repeat stack cursor.
Voice 2 command $CE. Counts down the active repeat. Returns to the saved position until it expires, then advances past this token.
Voice 2 command $D6. Copies five bytes from the embedded pointer into the envelope and waveform parameters.
Voice 2 command $D4. Copies fourteen instrument bytes from the embedded pointer.
Voice 2 command $D2. Copies ten instrument bytes into the voice synthesis parameters from the embedded pointer.
Voice 2 command $D0. Loads the pointed synthesis data using the command’s own index operands, then advances by five bytes.
Voice 2 command $C8. Updates the transposition from the fourth command byte and continues at the command target.
Voice 2 command $C4. Replaces the stream pointer with the little-endian target.
Voice 2 command $DA. Pushes the stream-advance return address and jumps indirectly to the machine-code routine named by the operands.
Voice 2 command $C6. Updates the transposition, saves a four-byte return address and changes the stream pointer.
Voice 2 command $C2. Saves a return position three bytes beyond the command and changes to the target stream.
Voice 2 command $DC. Stores the one-byte transposition and advances two bytes.
Voice 2 command $CA. Uses the first operand as an index into the voice’s instrument state and the second as the value.
Voice 2 command $D8. Writes the command value to the indexed effect parameter and advances three bytes.
Handles the active voice 2 effect counter and gate, writing voice 2 SID registers when the effect calls for changes.
Tests the voice 2 pitch-ramp flags to decide whether to restart with the saved pitch or reload the current ramp counts.
The operand for the ramp restart mask. The following branch selects the voice 2 pitch update or reload path.
Decrements voice 3's music duration and fetches another event when due, servicing the effect channel in between.
Low operand of the jump that dispatches voice 3 song events.
High operand byte in the voice 3 command jump. The following note path resolves the event into the note frequency and voice 3 setup.
Voice 3 command $C0. Pops a stream frame, restoring the saved address or clearing the voice playing flag when the stack is empty.
Voice 3 command $CC. Saves a repeat count and a stream return position, then changes the repeat stack cursor.
Voice 3 command $CE. Counts down the active repeat. Returns to the saved position until it expires, then advances past this token.
Voice 3 command $D6. Copies five bytes from the embedded pointer into the envelope and waveform parameters.
Voice 3 command $D4. Copies fourteen instrument bytes from the embedded pointer.
Voice 3 command $D2. Copies ten instrument bytes into the voice synthesis parameters from the embedded pointer.
Voice 3 command $D0. Loads the pointed synthesis data using the command’s own index operands, then advances by five bytes.
Voice 3 command $C8. Updates the transposition from the fourth command byte and continues at the command target.
Voice 3 command $C4. Replaces the stream pointer with the little-endian target.
Voice 3 command $DA. Pushes the stream-advance return address and jumps indirectly to the machine-code routine named by the operands.
Voice 3 command $C6. Updates the transposition, saves a four-byte return address and changes the stream pointer.
Voice 3 command $C2. Saves a return position three bytes beyond the command and changes to the target stream.
Voice 3 command $DC. Stores the one-byte transposition and advances two bytes.
Voice 3 command $CA. Uses the first operand as an index into the voice’s instrument state and the second as the value.
Voice 3 command $D8. Writes the command value to the indexed effect parameter and advances three bytes.
Handles the effect lifetime and gate transitions for voice 3, then updates oscillator state while the event remains active.
Base operand at $837B, used with Y=$F2–$FF to address the fourteen bytes starting at $8C28. The address itself lies on a voice 3 oscillator instruction.
Base operand used from $8695 with Y=$F2–$FF, giving the actual voice 2 synthesis source at $8C5D.
Base operand used from $89AE with Y=$F2–$FF, giving the actual voice 3 synthesis source at $8C92.
Base operand at $837E. Indexing with Y=$F2–$FF makes the store target the fourteen bytes at $8CD7–$8CE4.
Base operand at $8698. Indexing with Y=$F2–$FF makes the store target $8CFE–$8D0B.
Voice 1 working parameters for its waveform, envelope and note modulation. Stream commands update this block from pointed instrument data.
Eight low return-address bytes, eight high return-address bytes, and eight repeat counters for voice 1.
Voice 2 working modulation parameters and repeat state. $87A9 writes to the first parameter array.
Voice 3 working modulation parameters and repeat state. $8AC2 writes to the first parameter array.
End of the voice 3 repeat stack arrays, which hold return pointers and repeat counts.
Voice 1 synthesis parameters copied into the current effect state, followed by the frequency, gate and effect lifetime fields.
Voice 2 copy of the current effect parameters and its pitch, gate and timing fields.
Voice 3 copy of the current effect parameters, oscillator ramp and lifetime fields.
One note transposition per stream, added before the SID frequency lookup.
Three flags controlling whether the respective music voice fetches and advances note events.
Per-voice state used by the note path before applying the voice's own SID registers.
Voice restart mask followed by cached cutoff, filter resonance, mode and volume fields.
Offset bases used to map voice indices to their working state and their SID register groups.
The high bytes of the ascending 16-bit SID note frequencies. Indexed alongside $8DC3 after decoding the note and transposition.

Takes a sprite index in X, reads its shape pointer from $A00C,X and multiplies it by 64 within VIC bank $4000. Returns the address in $F0/$F1.
Computes a byte for each value of X by reversing the order of its four two-bit pairs, storing the result at $C274,X.
Reads CIA1's port A direction register using LAX and expects $E0. A mismatch writes $30 to the CPU port, banking out the I/O area.
Installs the raster IRQ, decodes initial screen data, and clears the session's per-player state before configuring the VIC-II sprites and starting the fight loop.
Clears active sound, resets the panel flash divider and passes control to the round-entry and fight setup paths.
Tests the sprite-bank marker at $203F against the opponent group. Calls the first memory exchange when the bank and the fight's group disagree.
Draws the KO bars, panel numbers and opponent label, selects the needed sprite bank, and loads the parameters for the current opponent.
Chooses whether to show the opponent preview or enter the next fight. In a two-player session it can hand a completed player's result to the front end before changing turns.
Standalone RTS before the short alternate restore path.
Uses the player index in A to load that player's lives and stage. A negative life count branches into the return-to-front-end path.
Discards two return addresses, passes stage and player in A and X, and returns with interrupts disabled.
Enters the final-return path for a negative lives count. Otherwise restores the opponent preview and multicolor sprite selection.
Blanks the screen, draws the panel, sets the temporary preview index $F3, decodes the preview screen and restores display output.
Adds the screen-code base for 1 to the player index and writes the panel's player number at $4008.
Reduces the current opponent index to a position within its group of five and clears the earlier cards' graphic cells.
Looks up the card destination and paints four blank cells on each of five rows.
Five pointers to the cells for the cards in each group of five opponents.
Offsets of the successive 40-column card rows from the card’s screen address.
Loads the current opponent index then uses the indexed name path at $BFD4.
Selects the name record from the table at $C00C and passes it to the panel text copier.
Uses the argument to choose one of the message addresses at $BFF4 and passes it to $C131.
Two pointers passed to the addressed string copier. Selects PERFECT or the blank row.
The screen address followed by PERFECT and a negative terminator.
Addressed string of spaces ending in $FF. Replaces the PERFECT text at the same target.
Sixteen pointers to addressed text records. The first ten select individual names; the remainder hold preview headings and rows.
High-byte base of the addressed string table used by the indexed panel text entry.
Addressed label for screen address $4070 with text 'BUCHU'. A negative byte ends the copy.

Uses the first two record bytes as the screen destination. Copies subsequent nonnegative characters with codes above $3F reduced by $40.
Low byte of the screen destination patched from the start of each addressed text record.
High byte of the screen destination patched from the start of each addressed text record.
For the early stages, updates a divider and rotates tile codes among fixed screen positions in the waterfall strip.
Chooses the group of three fighter sprites that faces the other way and calls the three per-slot reflection copiers.
Reverses the order of the three bytes in each row and the four two-bit pixel pairs in each byte into sprite storage at $6F40.
Reads the source rows backward and maps each byte through $C274 while writing the three columns in reversed order into the reflection buffer.
Picks the source through the slot used for the weapon, then reflects its pixel pairs and byte order into $6EC0.
All 256 possible eight-bit rows with the order of their four two-bit pixels reversed. Initialized at $BD08 and used when copying reflected fighter sprites.
Installs $C3A7 in the hardware IRQ vector, enables raster IRQ on line $C8, disables CIA1 IRQ sources and sets the CPU port to $35 before enabling interrupts.
Saves registers, acknowledges the VIC-II raster interrupt, calls the phase routine, selects the next routine from $C3F9, acknowledges CIA1 and returns from interrupt.
Low operand of the current raster phase JSR.
High byte of the self-modifying IRQ subroutine operand. The remainder of the dispatcher updates the next phase and restores the interrupted registers.
The first raster phase index outside each of the three phase groups. Equality advances the phase cursor to the reset value from $C3F6.
Phase restart indices for the early stage, later stage and preview groups, respectively.
IRQ subroutine targets indexed by the raster phase. Copied into the operand at $C3BC/$C3BD.
High-byte base paired with $C3F9 in the phase table.
Selects light blue background and schedules the next raster IRQ at $F0. Calls $C156 before returning to the IRQ dispatcher.
Selects light blue background and schedules the next raster IRQ at $C2.
Reuses a sprite below the main fighter band. Sets its Y coordinate, pointer, color and single-color mode before scheduling the next IRQ at $FF.
Refreshes the preview pose and sprite coordinates, then schedules line $F0.
Adds a fight tick, sets panel colors, refreshes preview sprites, restores the $7000 charset and schedules the next IRQ at $4A.
Adds a fight tick, restores panel colors and the $7000 charset, and schedules the next IRQ at $4A.
Sets the playfield color registers, selects multicolor for sprites 2–7, switches the VIC-II character base to $7800 and schedules IRQ line $69.
Selects the preview's lower-band colors and sprite multicolor 1 and schedules IRQ line $99.
Sets the playfield background and multicolor registers, enables multicolor on sprites 2–7 and schedules the next raster interrupt for line $72.
Sets background 0 to $0B and next raster line to $81.
Sets background 0 to $0E and next raster line to $89.
Writes $00/$00/$09 to the three background registers and schedules line $A1.
Writes $0D/$00/$0C to the three background registers and schedules line $B1.
Writes $0E/$00/$0C to the three background registers and schedules line $C1.
Writes $08/$00/$0E to the three background registers and schedules line $F0.
Adds one to the zero-based stage in decimal mode and writes its two screen-code digits into $401B/$401C.
Starts from nine and subtracts the live counter, using the result to select how many of the lives cells show their filled glyph.
Writes spaces into the runs around the live icons at $4046.
Three BCD bytes holding the award to add to the player's score. The low byte is reset after the addition.
Adds three BCD bytes with decimal carry to $0380–$0382, then restores binary arithmetic.
Expands the player's three BCD pairs into six screen-code digits at $402A.
Gets the three packed high-score bytes from $040B and writes the two screen digits from each to $4034 onward.
Watches bit 1 of the highest BCD score byte, ignores the transition addressed by its branch and adds one life if the count is below eight. Plays a cue and refreshes the icons.
Offsets into the sound dispatch table used by the hit paths to select cues for pose indices.
One byte per title bitmap cell in row-major order. $0B80 copies the low nibble to color RAM for multicolor selector 11.
Second source page copied into color RAM. It begins at the 257th title bitmap cell.
Third source page of per-cell selector 11 colors, beginning at the 513th bitmap cell.
Final source page of selector 11 colors, beginning at the 769th cell. The final 24 bytes are outside the visible color plane.
Last 24 bytes in the four-page source copied into color RAM by the title initializer. The title displays 1000 cells.
One byte per title bitmap cell in row-major order, with foreground colors in the high and low nibbles for multicolor selectors 01 and 10.
The 24 bytes in the title screen attribute page past its 1000 visible cells. The bitmap title disables the sprite display.
First kilobyte of the under-I/O tape block, copied to $A000–$A3FF before entering the game. The destination starts with the jump to fight initialization and includes the fight loop and its state.
Second kilobyte of turbo block 8. The loader copies these bytes under SID space to $A400–$A7FF, which includes collision checks and the opponent dispatch.
Third kilobyte of the block, copied from RAM beneath color RAM to $A800–$ABFF. This includes portions of several opponent behavior handlers.
Last kilobyte of the block, copied from RAM beneath the CIAs and expansion I/O to $AC00–$AFFF. This includes Pole and Nuncha behavior and part of Star's.
Title bitmap cell rows 0–2. Each 40-cell row takes 320 bytes, with eight two-bit-pixel scanlines together per cell.
